analysis: Reviewed the head_text excerpt (lines 4231-4689) of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. It is test-only code; no production behavior changes in the supplied unit. The tests exercise the sliding-window sidecar feature of the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, TB-007, A-001): corrupt-sidecar fail-closed handling (unlink and de-index, block adoption still stands), feature off by default, production donation path, replay-bound conservatism, write-budget priority of required blocks over optional sidecars (endurance), TTL refresh on re-donation, and a privacy check that the plaintext DBK3 header carries no absolute token position (only an opaque 64-hex HMAC commitment) and that the commitment binds the position against splicing. These tests reinforce the T-041 posture: HMAC-keyed names, no prompt-derived plaintext metadata beyond keyed tags, the 30-minute sliding TTL, and the endurance guard. The excerpt shows the plaintext header keeps a deliberate 'windowKind' discriminator, which the test documents as accepted and consistent with public architecture; this is not a new leak of prompt content. I identified no security regression in the tests. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the production sources (SSDPrefixCache, SSDWindowSidecar, SSDLookupKeys, SSDWholeRootMaintainer) are not supplied, so I could not verify that the production code matches what the tests assert. The first changed hunk (around lines 3140-3240, header-verdict memoization with ctime-based change detection in the whole-root maintainer) is outside this unit's visible text. The next pass should verify the production sidecar write/read paths against the T-041 detection hints: no new prompt-derived plaintext metadata, the TTL, and the AAD construction.
